revision_rule.note: The 2012 rule uses line-group productions and does not state the 2023 block-of-text termination and hidden-directive semantics.

The historical conditional-compilation rules use groups of lines and do not define the 2023 block_of_text termination rule or its explicit hiding of directive spellings in comments, strings, and macro definitions.
The 2012 grammar permits only a bare text macro identifier after `ifdef, `ifndef, and `elsif; it has no parenthesized condition-expression grammar or logical operators.
The historical grammar permits only a bare text macro identifier after `ifdef, `ifndef, and `elsif; it does not permit parenthesized macro expressions or the 2023 logical operators.
The 2012 conditional-compilation clause has no corresponding whitespace-insensitive block-termination guarantee.
The historical standard has no corresponding conditional-block termination whitespace guarantee.
The historical standard does not define processing versus suppression of compiler directives embedded in selected versus ignored conditional-compilation text.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no ifdef macro-expression construct or rule replacing identifiers with Boolean values for expression evaluation.
The historical standard has no ifdef_macro_expression construct or corresponding identifier-to-Boolean and logical-expression evaluation rule.
The 2012 branch-selection rule tests only bare text macro identifiers; parenthesized Boolean conditional expressions are not supported.
The historical rule selects the first successful branch using definedness of bare macro identifiers only; parenthesized conditional expressions are not supported.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no general rule permitting another language element after a terminated directive on the same line.
The historical standard has no general rule permitting a language element after a completed compiler directive on the same line.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no general guarantee permitting a language element before a directive on the same line.
The historical standard has no general rule permitting a language element before a compiler directive on the same line.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no general one-line requirement for all directives subject to directive-specific multiline exceptions.
The historical standard does not impose the 2023 general one-line rule across compiler directives; only directive-specific line rules are stated.
The 2012 rule gives `ifndef the inverse bare-identifier test but has no parenthesized condition expressions or whole-expression negation form.
The historical `ifndef rule is the inverse of bare macro definedness, but it has no parenthesized conditional-expression form to negate.
The 2012 syntax lists versions only through 1800-2012 and therefore does not accept the later 1800-2017 or 1800-2023 specifiers.
The historical standardized version list ends at 1800-2017 and does not accept the 1800-2023 version specifier.
IEEE 1800-2012 does not require every `begin_keywords to have a later `end_keywords; its selected set can remain active to the end of the compilation unit.
The historical standard allows a `begin_keywords region to continue to the end of the compilation unit, rather than requiring every `begin_keywords to be followed by a matching `end_keywords.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no 1800-2017 or 1800-2023 version specifier or corresponding later-version keyword-set guarantee.
The historical rule defines the cumulative 1800-2017 keyword set with no new words, but has no 1800-2023 version specifier or corresponding keyword-set guarantee.
The 2012 delimiter rule protects commas and right parentheses in matched delimiters, ordinary double-quoted strings, or escaped identifiers, but has no triple-quoted string form.

The historical delimiter rule protects commas and right parentheses inside matched delimiters, ordinary double-quoted strings, or escaped identifiers, but does not recognize the 2023 triple-quoted string form.
IEEE 1800-2012 states removal only for one-line comments and does not provide the later block-comment and line-comment continuation rules.
The historical rule removes a one-line comment from macro text but does not specify removal and unescaped-newline handling for multiline block comments or continuation after a line comment.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no rule delaying a compiler directive embedded in macro replacement text until macro use.
The historical standard does not define deferred processing of a compiler directive embedded in macro replacement text.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no general guarantee that macro invocations are expanded within compiler directives.
The historical standard has no general rule requiring macro expansion within a compiler directive while that directive is processed.
The 2012 rule requires the opening parenthesis to follow the macro name immediately and does not specify the later escaped-identifier terminating-space exception.

The historical rule requires the opening parenthesis to follow the macro name immediately and does not provide the 2023 exception allowing an escaped macro name's single terminating whitespace character.
The 2012 mixed-quote rule covers ordinary quote and grave-accent-quote forms only; triple-quoted literals and grave-accent-triple-quote forms are absent.
The historical rule covers mixing grave-accent quote with ordinary quote, but has no triple-quoted literal or grave-accent-triple-quote forms.
IEEE 1800-2012 generally preserves the newline while removing the continuation backslash and does not state the later string-literal exception that removes both characters.
The historical macro continuation rule replaces backslash-newline with a newline generally and does not state the 2023 string-literal exception that omits both characters.
The 2012 rule ends macro text at the first unescaped newline and has no exceptions for block comments or triple-quoted strings.
The historical rule ends macro text at the first unescaped newline without the 2023 exceptions for newlines inside block comments and triple-quoted strings.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no grave-accent-triple-quote macro operator or associated newline behavior.
The historical standard has no grave-accent-triple-quote macro operator or triple-quoted string construction.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no triple-quoted string literal and therefore no macro-definition newline exception for that construct.
The historical standard has no triple-quoted string literal form and therefore no rule allowing its internal newlines in macro text.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no general prohibition on a compiler directive occurring in the middle of another directive with a macro-use exception.
The historical standard has no general prohibition on recognizing one compiler directive in the middle of another or the associated macro-usage exception.
IEEE 1800-2012 does not state the corresponding compiler-directive recognition guarantee for directive spellings inside comments or string literals.
The historical standard has no corresponding explicit compiler-directive recognition rule for directive spellings inside comments or string literals.
The include-context save, restoration, and line/file update rules are stated in 22.12; the predefined macros in 22.13 expose that maintained state.
IEEE 1800-2012 does not prohibit a `timescale directive from appearing within a design element.
The historical `timescale clause does not prohibit placement of the directive within a design element.
